lines: {target}? Bright trunks can make shadows easy to miss. I would help whoever is closest.
If anyone heads for Birch Forest, tell them: Don't let the pretty light lower your guard. I will be at the square.
White bark shows marks, but not always danger. I'll keep that in mind by the square.
Birch Forest is no small story. A village survives by hands, not titles.
I will remember Birch Forest as a pale forest with quiet steps under it. I will keep my hands free to help.
{target}? I would not rush toward it without telling someone where you are going first.
That kind of place makes a simple walk feel like a decision. Pack food, count your torches, and keep your head clear.
I have heard enough about {target} to know the quiet parts are usually the ones to worry about.
If you go there, come back with the story and not just the scratches. The village remembers both.
A place like {target} can turn confidence into <shake>panic</shake> very quickly.
